statement: You are given an undirected graph, made of a vertex count n (vertices numbered 0 to n − 1) and a list of edges [u, v].

Two vertices are in the same connected component when a path of edges leads from one to the other. A component is as large as possible: no edge leaves it. A vertex with no edges is a component by itself.
Return the number of connected components. Scan the vertices in order and start a depth-first search from each vertex that no earlier search has reached; each such start discovers one new component.

examples.explanation: The components are {0, 1, 2}, {3, 4, 5} and the isolated vertex {6}.
The edges form one ring through all six vertices, so a single search from vertex 0 reaches everything.
